claims.text: The initial material is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast alloy has a fine, regular lamellar microstructure consisting of alternating fcc and B2 phases.
The fcc lamellae are soft and Co/Cr/Fe-rich, whereas the B2 lamellae are hard and NiAl-rich.
The as-cast alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Hydrostatic pressure above 20 GPa at 600–800°C will induce a localized polymorphic transition in the B2 lamellae.
The pressure-induced product in the B2 lamellae will be hcp-like or a distorted B2 structure.
Partial transformation will disrupt the continuous brittle B2 network.
The transformed configuration will modify interfacial energy and reduce the elastic-modulus mismatch between the phases.
A pressure window of approximately 22–41 GPa is appropriate for inducing the proposed transition in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
A temperature window of 600–800°C is below the eutectic reaction temperature and high enough to facilitate transformation kinetics without destroying structural integrity.
Controlled decompression will help retain the metastable transformed configuration.
In CoCrFeMnNi, hydrostatic pressure overcomes kinetic barriers and produces an fcc-to-hcp transition beginning near 22 GPa and completing near 41 GPa.
The pressure-driven fcc-to-hcp mechanism in CoCrFeMnNi is applicable by analogy to the B2 lamellae of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Elevated temperature will facilitate the atomic stacking rearrangement needed for the proposed B2-to-hcp-like transformation.
The transformed B2-derived phase will have lower stacking-fault energy or different slip systems than the original B2 phase.
The transformed interfaces will promote dislocation storage and nanotwinning rather than brittle cleavage, thereby reducing stress concentration.
The treatment will produce a patterned microstructure in which B2 lamellae are partially transformed.
The treated alloy will show reduced interfacial cracking and increased uniform elongation.
The treatment will maintain or enhance yield strength through a composite effect between the transformed hard phase and the soft fcc matrix.
Below 20 GPa, no relevant transformation will occur and the alloy will remain brittle.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention describe pressure merely exceeding 20 GPa as sufficient, whereas the conditions and boundary state that success requires approximately 22 GPa or more, leaving the 20–22 GPa interval inconsistently classified.
